e5 — Open Game. Both sides fight for the center. It leads to sharp, tactical games.

Nc3 — Four Knights Game. 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 Nf6. Both sides bring both knights out — a calm, classical, very safe way to play 1.e4. Aim the bishop at b5 (Spanish-style), castle, and play a sound game with a tiny edge from the extra move.

Nf6 — watch out, you've walked into Halloween Gambit territory. White gives up a knight for one pawn but gets a huge pawn center with d4-d5-e5. Black's pieces get pushed all the way back to the starting squares. After Nxe5, play Nc6 then Bb4 to pin the knight. Black keeps the extra piece. The punisher will play Nxe5 next.

d6 — Italian Game (Black side). How to defend against the Italian Game (1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4) as Black.
